page: Amazon Web Services a1.metal is a bare-metal instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. Built on the 64-bit Arm Neoverse Cortex-A72 architecture, it provides 16 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at 2.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core cluster, with hardware cryptographic acceleration via ARMv8 Cryptography extensions. The instance features no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, contains no GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the characteristics of early Arm-based server architecture. Synthetic CPU performance shows solid parallelism, with stress-ng multi-core achieving 24,102.93 and Clang software compilation reaching 6,794.0 in Geekbench. In-memory key-value processing is stable, yielding 8.6 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. However, single-threaded processing reflects architectural limitations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 418.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 10.09 GB/sec. Large uncached memory writes drop to 10.05 GB/sec, while L1/L2 cached small block memory reads reach 572.2 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput measured 3.68 GB/sec.

The absence of a virtualization hypervisor on a1.metal eliminates virtualization overhead, granting direct low-level access to the Cortex-A72 processor execution pipeline. While per-core compute output is modest compared to contemporary architectures, the 16 physical cores offer predictable parallel execution. This configuration delivers resource efficiency for distributed scale-out architectures, Arm64 application testing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, containerized microservices, and web tier deployments that do not rely on high single-thread clock rates or local high-IOPS storage.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.metal is a bare-metal instance built on the first-generation AWS Graviton architecture with 16 dedicated Arm Cortex-A72 physical cores running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for data persistence. Benchmark data reflects moderate multi-core throughput, recording 24,102.93 on stress-ng and 8.6 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, balanced against restrained single-thread and memory write speeds. Direct bare-metal access eliminates hypervisor latency, offering predictable execution across dedicated execution threads. This instance profile is engineered for Arm64 binary validation, containerized web applications, CI/CD build environments, and distributed scale-out workloads.
